results.title: Cubic-recurrence discriminant sequence

results.title: Divisibility of the cubic-recurrence discriminants
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $S_1, S_2, R$ be integers, let $U$ and $W$ be integer sequences forming a cubic recurrence pair for $(S_1, S_2, R)$, and let $D_n = \gcd(W_n - 6R^n, U_n)$ be their discriminant sequence. Then for all integers $n \ge 1$ and $m \ge 1$, $D_n$ divides $D_{nm}$.

results.title: Square Pell–Lucas numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the Pell–Lucas number $Q_n$ is a perfect square if and only if $n = 0$ or $n = 1$; thus the only square terms of the sequence are $Q_0 = Q_1 = 1$.

results.title: Pell and Pell–Lucas numbers are coprime
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the Pell number $P_n$ and the Pell–Lucas number $Q_n$ satisfy $\gcd(P_n, Q_n) = 1$.

results.title: Consecutive Pell–Lucas numbers are coprime
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the Pell–Lucas numbers $Q_n$ and $Q_{n+1}$ satisfy $\gcd(Q_n, Q_{n+1}) = 1$.

results.title: Sums of two coprime positive $n$-th powers are not squares for $n \ge 4$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n \ge 4$ be a natural number and let $x$ and $y$ be coprime positive integers. Then $x^n + y^n$ is not a perfect square: there is no natural number $z$ with $x^n + y^n = z^2$.

results.title: Sums of powers of consecutive Pell–Lucas numbers that are squares
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $Q_n$ denote the Pell–Lucas numbers. For natural numbers $n$, $x$ and $y$, the equation $Q_n^x + Q_{n+1}^x = y^2$ holds if and only if $n = 1$, $x = 1$ and $y = 2$; that is, its only solution in natural numbers is $Q_1 + Q_2 = 1 + 3 = 2^2$.

results.title: Geometric sums for primes $p \equiv 3 \pmod 4$ and odd $n$ are sums of two squares
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime with $p \equiv 3 \pmod 4$, let $n$ be a positive odd integer, and let $S = \sum_{j=0}^{p-1} p^{nj} = 1 + p^n + p^{2n} + \cdots + p^{(p-1)n}$. Then every prime divisor of $S$ is $2$ or congruent to $1$ modulo $4$, and there are natural numbers $a, b$ with $S = a^2 + b^2$.

results.title: An alternating sum in coprime integers $x, y$ is a sum of two coprime squares
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $x$ and $y$ be coprime integers, let $n$ be a positive integer, and let $S = \sum_{j=0}^{2n} (-1)^j x^{4n-2j} y^{2j}$, that is, $S = x^{4n} - x^{4n-2} y^2 + \cdots - x^2 y^{4n-2} + y^{4n}$. Then every prime divisor of $S$ is $2$ or congruent to $1$ modulo $4$, and there are coprime natural numbers $a, b$ with $S = a^2 + b^2$.

results.title: Hypergeometric mass function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The hypergeometric mass function: the probability `C(K, k) C(N - K, n - k) / C(N, n)` of drawing exactly `k` marked items in `n` draws without replacement from `N` items of which `K` are marked; it is `0` for `k > n`. The parameter domain is `K ≤ N`, `n ≤ N`; outside it the value is not a probability (`N - K` truncates, and `C(N, n) = 0` makes it `0` for `n > N`).

results.title: $k$-abelian squares
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $k$, a word $w$ is a $k$-abelian square when $w = uv$ for two nonempty words $u$ and $v$ that are $k$-abelian equivalent.

results.title: $k$-abelian square-free words
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $k$, a finite word $w$ is $k$-abelian square-free when $k \ge 1$ and no factor of $w$ (a word $x$ with $w = pxs$ for some words $p$ and $s$) is a $k$-abelian square.

results.title: $3$-abelian equivalence of ternary words
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Two words $u$ and $v$ over the alphabet $\{0, 1, 2\}$ are $3$-abelian equivalent when they are $k$-abelian equivalent for $k = 3$: both are nonempty, they have the same prefix and the same suffix of length $2$ (a shorter word counting as its own prefix and suffix), and every word of length $3$ occurs as a factor of $u$, counting overlapping occurrences, exactly as often as it occurs in $v$.

results.title: $3$-abelian squares over a ternary alphabet

results.summary: A word $w$ over the alphabet $\{0, 1, 2\}$ is a $3$-abelian square when $w = uv$ for two nonempty words $u$ and $v$ that are $3$-abelian equivalent.

results.title: $3$-abelian square-free ternary words

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The sojourn density is continuous in the starting frequency (in particular at `p = x`).

results.title: Left derivative of the sojourn density at the diagonal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Left derivative at the diagonal: `∂_p Ψ(x⁻, x) = 2 (1 - u(x)) / (x (1 - x))`. Together with `hasDerivWithinAt_selectionGreen_Ici` this gives the jump `-2 / (x (1 - x))` of `∂_p Ψ` at `p = x`, i.e. `L_σ Ψ(·, x) = -δ_x` in the distributional sense.

results.title: Right derivative of the sojourn density at the diagonal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Right derivative at the diagonal: `∂_p Ψ(x⁺, x) = -2 u(x) / (x (1 - x))`.

results.title: Maruyama–Kimura conditional sojourn density
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Maruyama–Kimura conditional sojourn density (the paper's `Ψ_z(p, z)`): given the initial frequency `p` and the current frequency `x`, the density of mean time spent at frequency `z` along the path, `Ψ(p, z) Ψ(z, x) / Ψ(p, x)` (Maruyama and Kimura 1975; Kiezun et al. 2013, Methods). Time in units of `2N` generations.

results.title: Closed-form sojourn density below the current frequency
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The paper's closed form `Ψ₁(z)` for `0 < z < x` (Kiezun et al. 2013, Methods), in units of `2N` generations with `σ = 2Ns`: `(e^{-2σ(1-z)} - 1)(e^{-2σz} - 1) / (σ z (1 - z) (1 - e^{-2σ}))`, and its continuous extension `2` for `σ = 0`. It does not depend on the current frequency `x`.

results.title: Closed-form sojourn density above the current frequency
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The paper's closed form `Ψ₂(z)` for `x < z < 1` (Kiezun et al. 2013, Methods), in units of `2N` generations with `σ = 2Ns`: `(e^{-2σ(1-z)} - 1)(e^{2σ(1-z)} - 1)(1 - e^{2σx}) / (σ z (1 - z)(e^{-2σ(1-x)} - 1)(1 - e^{2σ}))`, and its continuous extension `2 x (1 - z) / ((1 - x) z)` for `σ = 0`.

results.title: Mean age of an allele at a given frequency
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The mean age of an allele at current frequency `x` (the paper's `a(x)`), in units of `2N` generations: `∫₀^x Ψ₁(z) dz + ∫_x^1 Ψ₂(z) dz`.

results.title: Sojourn density below the current frequency via fixation probability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `Ψ₁` through Kimura's fixation probability: `Ψ₁(z) = 2 u(z)(1 - u(z)) / (z (1 - z) u'(z))` on `(0, 1)`.

results.title: Sojourn density above the current frequency via fixation probability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `Ψ₂` through Kimura's fixation probability: `Ψ₂(z) = 2 u(x)(1 - u(z))² / ((1 - u(x)) z (1 - z) u'(z))` on `(0, 1)`.

results.title: Closed form below the current frequency
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `0 < p ≤ z ≤ x < 1` the conditional sojourn density is the paper's `Ψ₁(z)`; it depends neither on `p` nor on `x`.

results.title: Closed form above the current frequency
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `0 < p ≤ x ≤ z < 1` the conditional sojourn density is the paper's `Ψ₂(z)`; it does not depend on `p`.

results.title: Paper units
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: With `N` diploid individuals, selection coefficient `s ≠ 0` and time in generations, the paper prints `Ψ₁(z) = (e^{-γ(1-z)} - 1)(e^{-γz} - 1) / (s z (1 - z)(1 - e^{-γ}))` with `γ = 4Ns`; it equals `2N · maruyamaBelow (2Ns) z`.

results.title: Paper units
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The paper's `Ψ₂(z) = (e^{-γ(1-z)} - 1)(e^{γ(1-z)} - 1)(1 - e^{γx}) / (s z (1 - z)(e^{-γ(1-x)} - 1)(1 - e^{γ}))`, `γ = 4Ns`, equals `2N · maruyamaAbove (2Ns) x z`.

results.title: Kimura and Ohta (1973)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The mean age of a neutral allele at frequency `x ∈ (0, 1)` is `-2 x log x / (1 - x)` in units of `2N` generations (`-4N x ln x / (1 - x)` generations).

results.title: Hyperbolic form of the sojourn density below the current frequency
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `Ψ₁` in hyperbolic form: `2 sinh(σz) sinh(σ(1 - z)) / (σ z (1 - z) sinh σ)` for `σ ≠ 0`.

results.title: Hyperbolic form of the sojourn density above the current frequency
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `Ψ₂` in hyperbolic form: `2 sinh(σ(1 - z))² sinh(σx) / (σ sinh σ sinh(σ(1 - x)) z (1 - z))` for `σ ≠ 0`.

results.title: Symmetry
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `Ψ₁` is the same for `σ` and `-σ`.

results.title: Symmetry
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `Ψ₂` is the same for `σ` and `-σ`.

results.title: Positivity of the sojourn density below the current frequency
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `Ψ₁` is positive on `(0, 1)`.

results.title: Maruyama effect, below the current frequency
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `σ ≠ 0`, `Ψ₁(z) < 2`, its neutral value, for every `z ∈ (0, 1)`.

results.title: Maruyama effect, above the current frequency
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `σ ≠ 0` and `0 < x < z < 1`, `Ψ₂(z)` is strictly below its neutral value `2 x (1 - z) / ((1 - x) z)`.

results.title: Positivity of the sojourn density above the current frequency
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `Ψ₂` is positive for `0 < x < z < 1`.

results.title: Sojourn density above the current frequency vanishes at one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: At `z = 1` the closed form `Ψ₂` vanishes (a null set for the integral).

results.title: Integrability of the sojourn density below the current frequency
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `Ψ₁` is integrable on `[0, x]` (it is bounded by `2`).

results.title: Integrability of the sojourn density above the current frequency
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `Ψ₂` is integrable on `[x, 1]` for `x ∈ (0, 1)` (it is bounded by `2 / (1 - x)`).

results.title: Symmetry
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The mean age is the same for `σ` and `-σ`.

results.title: The Maruyama effect (Kiezun et al. 2013)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `σ ≠ 0` and `x ∈ (0, 1)`, an allele under selection, advantageous or deleterious, is on average strictly younger than a neutral allele at the same frequency.

results.title: Mean age as the limit of conditional sojourn times
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Mean age as the limit of conditional sojourn times (Maruyama 1974; Kiezun et al. 2013, Methods): for `x ∈ (0, 1)`, the total conditional sojourn time `∫₀¹ Ψ_z(p, z) dz` of a path from initial frequency `p` to current frequency `x` tends to the mean age `a(x)` as `p → 0⁺` (an allele arises at frequency close to `0`).

results.title: Stronger selection, smaller `Ψ₁`
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `0 ≤ σ < τ` and `z ∈ (0, 1)`, `Ψ₁` at `τ` is strictly below `Ψ₁` at `σ`.

results.title: Stronger selection, smaller `Ψ₂`
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `0 ≤ σ < τ` and `0 < x < z < 1`, `Ψ₂` at `τ` is strictly below `Ψ₂` at `σ`.

results.title: Stronger selection, younger alleles
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: At a fixed frequency `x ∈ (0, 1)`, the mean age is strictly decreasing in `σ ≥ 0`. Kiezun et al. (2013, Figure 1b) show this numerically from the closed forms; here it is proved.

results.title: Stronger selection, younger alleles
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Stronger selection, younger alleles, for either sign of selection: if `|σ| < |τ|` then an allele at frequency `x ∈ (0, 1)` under selection `τ` is on average strictly younger than one under selection `σ`.

results.title: Mean time as a sum of sojourn times
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Mean time as a sum of sojourn times (the identity behind Maruyama and Kimura 1975). For a jointly measurable family of transition densities `w p x t ≥ 0` on `(0, 1)` satisfying the Chapman–Kolmogorov equation for positive times, `∫₀^∞ t w(p, x, t) dt = ∫₀¹ Ψ(p, y) Ψ(y, x) dy` with `Ψ(p, x) = ∫₀^∞ w(p, x, t) dt`, in `ℝ≥0∞`.
